methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on the functional requirements of the shift register, including the number of flip-flops, reset behavior, input, and output. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on the header, combinational logic function, enhanced combinational description, interface behavior, timing dependency and timing logic.
spec_atomic_units: resetn resets the shift register to zero on the rising edge of clk
input in is sampled and shifted into the register on the rising edge of clk when resetn is high
output out reflects the value of the last flip-flop in the shift register chain
resetn must be stable before the rising edge of clk
input in must also be stable a setup time before the rising edge of clk
output out will be valid after a propagation delay from the rising edge of clk
circuit is a sequential circuit with four D flip-flops
flip-flops are triggered by the rising edge of the clk signal
register is reset only on the rising edge of clk when resetn is low
shift register shifts the data one bit position to the right on each rising edge of clk when resetn is high
out signal is the output of the last flip-flop in the shift register
